conflict_resolutions.EMPTY_CATALOG_NOTE_DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH_CU: The Federal Register catalog observation for Executive Order 13593 has an empty disposition note. An empty note neither shows the order is in force nor that it ended, and it is not used as a basis. I searched held texts for the number 13593 (the order's own text and Federal Register documents 2011-32486, 2012-25852, 2013-07804, 2016-06403 and 2016-21874, which publish, cite or annotate it and do not revoke or supersede it) and read the held original in full, including the Annex. The status rests on the order's own terms: its commands are self-executing amendments of the Manual for Courts-Martial that took effect on January 12, 2012, with no continuing command.

notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: Executive Order 13593 (December 13, 2011; 76 FR 78451) amends Parts III and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, as described in an Annex, effective 30 days after the date of the order (January 12, 2012). The held original was read in full: the order has no continuing duty, report or standing command, and Sec. 2(a) and (b) are rules of construction limiting the amendments' application to earlier conduct and proceedings. The amended text lives in the Manual (prescribed by Executive Order 12473, as amended), which is a separate instrument. The order's own commands were therefore complete on January 12, 2012. Recommended provisional status: no, on the order's own terms; the surviving amended Manual text and preserved earlier proceedings are carried under savings.
